clue.text: Bloom lady-killer put back in buttonhole

indicators.note: in places the reversed lady-killer inside the word for buttonhole

parts.note: to buttonhole someone is to corner them and make them listen

indicators.note: put back signals the word for the lady-killer is read in reverse

parts.note: a wolf is a man who preys on women

explanation.surface: A womaniser has tucked a flower into his lapel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lady-killer' looks like the definition of a person, but it supplies a womaniser's nickname; 'buttonhole' is a verb sense, to corner someone, not a flower in a lapel.
explanation.definitionFit: The blue wild flower of cornfields is a bloom, an example of the general term.

clue.text: American people given care of 70% of city

parts.note: c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of
the English city Manchester has ten letters, and seventy per cent of it is its first seven

explanation.surface: A Native American tribe is put in the care of most of an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: MANCHESTER, the English city, has ten letters, so 70% of it is the first seven, MANCHES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Comanche are a Native American nation of the southern Plains, so the plural names those people.

clue.text: They've made tracks and left wearing shortened garments

indicators.note: wearing puts the shortened garments around the abbreviation for left, as if clothing it
shortened says the word for garments loses its final letter

parts.note: raiment is an old word for clothing

explanation.surface: Someone ran off and departed dressed in clothes that were too short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' cuts RAIMENT to RAIMEN; 'wearing' wraps that round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway workers laid the lines, so they literally made tracks, while the phrase also means ran off.

clue.text: Lad dines out in part of airport

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of the two words are put out of order

explanation.surface: A young man goes out to eat at the airport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LADDINES.
explanation.definitionFit: The landside is the area of an airport before security, open to the general public.

clue.text: Chant questioning restaurant staff's raison d'étre?

definitions.meaning: a familiar impatient chant from a waiting crowd or audience
read literally, it asks why waiters exist at all, since serving at table is called waiting

explanation.surface: A crowd chants impatiently while diners ask what the waiters are for.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stock chant of impatience, and literally a query about the purpose of those whose job is waiting.

clue.text: Look for respect

definitions.meaning: to ... something is to look at it

explanation.surface: Seeking admiration from others.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb meaning gaze at and as a noun meaning esteem or high opinion.

clue.text: Pot for reheated meat and vegetables

definitions.meaning: pot is slang for cannabis, of which hashish is a form
a dish of chopped leftover meat and potatoes fried up again

explanation.surface: A cooking pot for warming up leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang shortening of hashish for cannabis, and the name of a fry-up dish of chopped leftovers.

clue.text: Top setter supplying solution

parts.note: a setter for the top of the head, i.e. something that fixes hair in place, supplied as a liquid; the surface suggests the best crossword compiler providing answers

explanation.surface: The finest crossword compiler is handing out the answers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' and 'solution' look like puzzle talk; here top is the head, setter is what holds a hairstyle, and solution is a liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacquer sprayed on the head holds a hairstyle set, and comes as a liquid solution in a can.

clue.text: Longing to have animals raised part of the capital

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters are read upwards, so the whole run is reversed

parts.note: a yen is a yearning or longing
pets are domestic animals

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to have animals brought up in a city district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns YENPETS into STEPNEY. STEPNEY is a district of East London.
explanation.definitionFit: This district lies in the East End of London, the British capital, so it is part of that city.

clue.text: Like young female swimmer saved by male

indicators.note: saved by means held inside, so the fish sits within the word for male

parts.note: manly means having qualities thought typical of a man
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A girl swimmer is rescued by a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' is a crossword staple for a fish; here the small freshwater ide, held within the adjective for male.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidenly means befitting a maiden, a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: When speaking, made fun of a group leader

indicators.note: When speaking says the phrase is heard rather than written

parts.note: guyed means ridiculed, and a said loosely sounds like 'er, so the phrase is heard as guyed her

explanation.surface: Someone mocked a leader during a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech 'guyed her' and the answer sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A Guider is an adult leader of a unit in the Girl Guides movement.

clue.text: Old soldiers retreating? Captain brought to book

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: men are soldiers, as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: Veteran troops fall back and their captain is court-martialled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns OMEN backwards. 'brought to book' suggests punishment but means put into a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's novel, a seafarer brought into fiction.

clue.text: Unexpected pair implicated in US-backed insurgency

indicators.note: backed means turned around, so the two letters are read in reverse
implicated in means involved inside, so the abbreviation goes within the word for revolt

parts.note: a rising is a rebellion or revolt

explanation.surface: Two people are caught up in an American-sponsored uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US-backed' reads as political description of the uprising, but 'backed' is a reversal signal acting on the two letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something surprising is unforeseen, which is what unexpected means.

clue.text: Teacher's instruction after question's answered without effort

definitions.meaning: once pupils raising hands have answered, the teacher tells them to lower them
to win this way is to win easily, as a jockey who drops his hands

explanation.surface: A classroom routine where the teacher tells pupils to lower their arms.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means easily or comfortably, from a jockey winning without urging the horse.

clue.text: Easing of hostilities ends prematurely around border, resulting in damage

indicators.note: around puts the shortened easing word around the word for border
ends prematurely means the word stops a letter early, losing its final letter

parts.note: détente is a relaxation of tension between nations
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A truce between nations collapses early at the frontier and causes harm.
explanation.walkthrough: The détente loses its final E ('ends prematurely') to give DETENT, which then goes around the edge word.
explanation.definitionFit: Detriment is harm or loss, a formal synonym for damage.

clue.text: Shows effect of strain in fights

definitions.meaning: a rope or nerves that fray are wearing thin under stress

explanation.surface: Someone under stress gets into scraps.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means wears thin under tension; as a plural noun it means brawls or skirmishes.

clue.text: In various parades ambassador's taken lead

indicators.note: In says the ambassador's letters go inside the rearranged parades
various suggests the letters of the word take a different arrangement

parts.note: HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador; the 's is has

explanation.surface: At several processions the envoy walks at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges PARADES as SPEARAD; His Excellency's abbreviation for an ambassador goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To spearhead a campaign is to lead it, being at its front.

clue.text: Means of transmitting messages installed in teleprinter commonly

indicators.note: installed in signals the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A messaging device is usually fitted in a teleprinter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'installed in' finds the answer running across 'teleprinter commonly'.
explanation.definitionFit: An intercom is an internal two-way communication system for passing messages.

clue.text: Dog brought back hares about end of hunt

indicators.note: about places the reversed word around the final letter of hunt
brought back means returned in reverse, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: to hare is to rush, so hares means zips

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A hound retrieves hares at the close of the chase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns ZIPS into SPIZ; 'about' puts it round T from 'end of hunt'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spitz is a breed type of dog with a pointed muzzle and curled tail.

clue.text: Academic at university has little time for penitent politician

parts.note: prof is short for professor
U is short for university
a mo is a moment, a short time

explanation.surface: A professor is too busy to spare a moment for a remorseful MP.
explanation.walkthrough: John Profumo, a British minister who resigned over the 1963 scandal, spent decades doing charity work in atonement.
explanation.definitionFit: Profumo resigned from government in disgrace and then devoted his life to charitable penance, so he is a remorseful statesman.

clue.text: Not quite enough to make up two teams for a game

definitions.text: Not quite enough to make up two teams
definitions.meaning: two football or cricket teams of eleven need twenty-two, so one fewer falls short
a card game also called pontoon or blackjack

explanation.surface: We are one player short of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: One short of the twenty-two needed for two elevens, and the name of the casino card game blackjack.

clue.text: Gothic script expert?

definitions.meaning: an old style of handwriting such as black letter
a veteran who has long experience

explanation.surface: A specialist in medieval lettering.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand means handwriting, so an archaic script is an old hand; the idiom also names a seasoned veteran.

clue.text: Find fault with endless razzmatazz at church

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: glitz is showy glamour

explanation.surface: Someone criticises the showy extravagance at a service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts GLITZ to GLIT; 'Find' and 'with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A glitch is a minor malfunction or flaw, a technical fault.

clue.text: Fascinating woman jailed after tussle about love and deception

indicators.note: about puts the rearranged letters around the words for love and deception
after a tussle the word is roughed up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the shape of O
a lie is a deception

explanation.surface: An alluring woman was locked up after a scuffle over a romance and a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after tussle' turns JAILED into JLAIDE, and 'about' puts it round OLIE.
explanation.definitionFit: This French term describes a woman attractive despite plain features, hence fascinating.

clue.text: German banker circulating two notes

indicators.note: circulating means going round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: re is a note of the sol-fa scale
do, or doh, is another note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A German financier is passing round a couple of banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulating' turns REDO backwards. 'banker' is a crossword joke for a river, which has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a river forming much of the German–Polish border, so a German thing with banks.

clue.text: Most appealing version of film is French

parts.note: a cut is an edited version, as in a director's cut
est is French for is

explanation.surface: The best-looking version of the movie is the French one.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutest is the superlative of cute, meaning the most charming or attractive.

clue.text: Undeveloped island on which explorer briefly lands

parts.note: inch is a Scottish word for a small island

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: Lawrence Oates was a member of Scott's Antarctic expedition

explanation.surface: A polar explorer makes landfall on an island in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts OATES to OATE. INCH, as in Inchcolm, is Scottish for island.
explanation.definitionFit: Inchoate means only just begun, rudimentary or not yet fully formed.

clue.text: Unconscious immediately after start of boxing match

indicators.note: immediately after puts the word for unconscious straight after the first letter
start of picks the first letter of the following word

parts.note: a boxer knocked out is out cold

explanation.surface: A boxer is knocked out just after the fight begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of boxing' gives B, and 'immediately after' puts OUT behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bout is a contest, especially a boxing or wrestling match.

clue.text: Having moral principles, objected to drunk being given precedence

indicators.note: being given precedence says the word for drunk comes first

parts.note: high means intoxicated
minded means disliked or objected to

explanation.surface: Someone disapproved of an intoxicated person being put first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given precedence' means placed in front, so the word for drunk comes before the word for objected to.
explanation.definitionFit: High-minded means having lofty ethical standards, being principled.
